name: William Nielsen
life: “I still remember giving a goal score to a passenger who had missed his stop.” People around Maré Coffee know William by a small Wednesday habit. William likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I put up a score on match days. The passengers started holding up their predictions on the return journey.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a washed violet jersey and a thin silver ring worn on a cord. William has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. William presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: William treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To publish a match score the passengers can see.
family: Cora Adair is William’s half-sibling. William keeps the photographs. Cora knows which ones can be shared. They enjoy remembering people in public and also know what it feels like to have a private afternoon turned into an anecdote for strangers. Asked about *The missing Sunday*, Cora says, “I arranged every important task. My father asked what hour I'd set aside to waste with him.”
connections: Aisha Ortiz. The passenger who recognized a teacher starts looking out for the match score.

reactions.response: William waits for the resident to give permission before a camera goes up.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: William asks the neighbor privately what they want, without treating their place as something for sale.
